problem.title: Which methods commute with a per-coordinate (distinct-order) Weil lift of a vector field
problem.user_statement: Notice that overloading each equation with a distinct jet arithmetic makes sense in theory and practice, which is not far from the analogous of expanding in Taylor series each term of a vector function around a distinct point and up to a different order. The question is, which methods do accept this kind of behavior? That is, which methods do accept distinct Weil lift per coordinate so that it coincides with the same method applied to the same distinct Weil lifts per coordinate of the vector field.
problem.current_statement: Round 3 claim (Lilith's single formalized proposal): Fix n>=2, a per-coordinate order vector D=(D_1,...,D_n), Weil algebra W_D = R[e_1,...,e_n]/(e_1^{D_1+1},...,e_n^{D_n+1}), and the per-coordinate Weil lift of a vector field L_D(F) as Round-1 candidate (a) index-blind projection (fixed as background, not reopened). A one-step method M produces an update map Phi_h^M[F] from finitely many evaluations of F, well-typed over any commutative R-algebra. Let T_D be the canonical (routing-free) Weil lift of an actual map via its real mixed partials. M commutes with L_D if M[L_D(F)] = T_D(Phi_h^M[F]) identically in W_D, for every admissible F, D, h, x_0. Test this on {explicit Euler, RK2, RK4, implicit Euler, exact-jet/truncated-Taylor method} on a coupled 2-coordinate system with D_1 != D_2 permitted: which methods satisfy the identity exactly, which fail, which hold only to some order in h, and is there a structural (B-series/elementary-differential-type) necessary/sufficient condition on M for exact commutation at every order D. Per rule 6.6, this claim's line closed after 3 consecutive gap-located+misframed rounds; work is now moving to a new claim (see below) per the user's direction. jt-percoord is paused, not abandoned -- its findings remain on record.
problem.intent: Determine which numerical/geometric integration methods are compatible with per-coordinate, possibly distinct-order jet arithmetic (naturality of the method with respect to the per-coordinate Weil lift), i.e. how the renaming/overloading-jet-arithmetic idea restricts the class of admissible methods, rather than studying the vector-field lift itself (that question was closed in Rounds 1-2).

settled_conventions.convention: Per-coordinate Weil lift reading: fix (a-full) -- the full, untruncated, presentation-independent multivariate Taylor expansion of F, evaluated at a W_D-point, with truncation arising automatically from the nilpotency of W_D's generators. Discard (a-trunc) (the literal coordinatewise cutoff at alpha_i <= D_i, shown in Round 3 to be an index-dependent routing rule that deletes W_D-nonzero terms and is not equivalent to (a-full) off the slice). Drop the 'per-output'/index-blind-projection-as-a-second-reading framing as non-local per the user's ruling.
settled_conventions.scope: Definitional convention only -- fixes which construction later rounds on jt-percoord (or its descendants) test. Does NOT itself establish that exact commutation holds for algebraically-presented methods under this convention; that remains an open substantive question MAGI may still test on any future claim that revisits it. Recorded per the user's explicit instruction that this be treated as a convention, not a proven result.
settled_conventions.basis: Round 3 findings (Melchior: (a-full) vs (a-trunc) diverge off-slice, exact witness given; user's own argument: independent per-coordinate symbols tensor to a single Weil algebra, and every Weil algebra is a quotient of a jet algebra, so per-coordinate extension is not a new kind of object under the (a-full) reading).
